items.text: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70–78 marketed range, and expanded the deal to about 980 million Class A shares from a planned 825 million, the AP reports. That raises roughly $81 billion, which the AP and CNBC describe as the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's roughly $75 billion in June. It values the company at about $1.5 trillion. Shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday, Nov 19. The AP notes that Anthropic is unprofitable on a GAAP basis, carries $6.2 billion of debt, and has signed about $900 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments.
items.notes: Some outlets give $81.3bn raised and others 'over $81bn'. The first trade had not happened at the time of writing (Nasdaq opens 15:30 Warsaw time).

items.text: The AP called the Alaska Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola on Tuesday evening (Alaska time). Late-counted ballots took her to about 50.1% of first-choice votes, so no ranked-choice tabulation is needed, Alaska Public Media reports. She unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. The AP says this was the last undecided Senate race of the midterms and leaves Democrats with a 56–44 majority after flipping nine GOP-held seats. Sullivan's campaign did not comment, after saying earlier it would wait for every legal vote to be counted and certified. State certification is slated for Nov 25.
items.notes: The call came after the Nov 18 log was compiled. NPR and NBC also report the win. Final certified totals are not yet published.

items.text: Minutes of the Oct 27–28 FOMC meeting, released Nov 18, show that 'almost all' officials judged further rate increases would likely be appropriate. XTB's summary of the minutes says a few officials floated a move larger than 25 basis points if inflation data disappoint. The Fed held rates at 3.75–4.00% in October, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a hike. Reuters says almost all participants discussed the risk that AI investment returns could disappoint. Most noted that AI-related debt has grown fast through complex, opaque financing, and a few worried that exposure is concentrated in a small number of firms. Markets fully price a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting.
items.notes: The full minutes page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20261028.htm) could not be fetched. The rate range, dissents and the 'more than 25bp' detail come from XTB's summary, not the primary text.

items.text: The S&P 500 slipped about 0.2% to 7,323.63 on Wednesday, its fifth straight loss. The Dow fell 561 points (1.1%) to about 50,198 and the Nasdaq rose 0.4%, according to CNBC figures relayed by Stock Titan. Nvidia closed down about 2.9%: it rose pre-market after its blowout results but gave up the gain. Health insurers dragged the Dow, with UnitedHealth down about 10% and Humana about 13% on a second day of selling over CMS's proposed anti-fraud audit rule. Hawkish Fed minutes also weighed on stocks.
items.notes: Closing levels are CNBC's 5:13 pm ET figures as relayed by Stock Titan.

items.text: CMS has proposed a broad anti-fraud rule called CRUSH (Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare), covering Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP and the ACA marketplace. The agency projects nearly $90 billion in federal savings over 2027–2036. Its centrepiece expands Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment (RADV) audits: findings from sampled records would be extrapolated across whole contracts back to payment year 2018, with no fee-for-service adjustment. CMS estimates recoveries of about $9 billion per payment year. The rule also tightens provider enrolment, broker oversight and overpayment-return deadlines, and comments are due Jan 19, 2027. Insurer stocks fell sharply on Nov 17–18, and analysts quoted by Beinsure expect legal challenges, since a court vacated an earlier RADV rule in 2025.
items.notes: Proposed around Nov 16, and only the market reaction falls in the window. The CMS primary text and Federal Register citation were not retrieved.

items.text: Sens. Maria Cantwell (D) and Mike Rounds (R) wrote to Jay Clayton, who chairs the White House Super Intelligence Task Force, warning that AI-enabled cyber threats are escalating faster than US defences. They asked for urgent protection of critical infrastructure and banks, faster rollout of AI defensive tools, and security standards for autonomous AI agents, Reuters reports. They cited a run of recent disruptions: a 24-hour Microsoft outage, the FAA ground stop, a United Airlines halt and a JPMorgan Chase processing bug. A day earlier, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told CNBC he was '98% certain' none of these was a cyberattack and blamed new technology layered on ageing systems. Reuters adds that the FAA has tied its ground stop to a single router at a remote Arkansas facility.
items.notes: Mullin's remarks were made on Nov 17. The Arkansas router detail comes from Reuters (Shepardson), while CBS earlier pointed to old Cisco routers. The two are consistent, but the FAA's final root cause is still not published.

items.text: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission released its 2026 annual report to Congress on Nov 18. Its themes include control of the 'AI tech stack' and China's use of data. TokenPost says the commission recommends penalties for companies that fail to report use of Chinese AI models, SEC risk disclosures for listed firms, and a bar on Chinese models in critical infrastructure and national-security uses without a security review. Separately, Reuters reported (via U.S. News) that the Treasury and the White House OSTP have discussed requiring US companies to list on their websites the Chinese models they use, without banning them. The proposal is still under discussion.
items.notes: The recommendations come from secondary coverage, because the report PDF was not reviewed. The Reuters exclusive on the administration's deliberations could not be fetched directly, and its details come from TokenPost and the headline.

items.text: Trump landed in Shenzhen on Nov 18 after the Manila leg. PBS NewsHour reports that Xi Jinping greeted him personally at the airport, a first for a foreign leader in Xi's 14 years in power, and that Putin was also there. The first-ever formal trilateral of the US, Chinese and Russian leaders is set for Nov 19 on the APEC sidelines, alongside a third Trump–Xi bilateral this year and separate Trump–Putin talks. No official agenda has been released. Trump wants a three-way nuclear arms-control deal, which officials and analysts say has low prospects. Iran, Ukraine, trade and AI are also expected to come up.
items.notes: An NBC live-blog headline says Trump sat down with Putin ahead of the three-way talks, but the page could not be read. The summit's outcomes were not available at the time of writing.

items.text: At a state luncheon hosted by President Marcos in Manila on Nov 18, Trump said the US and the Philippines had concluded 'the biggest trade deal' ever, and he pledged closer defence cooperation. He gave no terms. Philippine Ambassador Jose Manuel Romualdez said nothing had been signed and that the US had offered help diversifying food and energy supplies, the Daily Guardian reports. Marcos said the Pax Silica framework would not be signed on this trip.
items.notes: PBS NewsHour describes Trump as having 'signed' a deal with the Philippines, but the Philippine ambassador says nothing was signed.

items.text: Bahrain and Kuwait said they repelled air attacks on Wednesday, and Iran's army said it targeted Patriot air-defence systems at Kuwait's Ali Al-Salem air base, which hosts US forces, CBS News reports. A UAE ADNOC vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one crew member missing and 11 injured. CENTCOM said no US personnel were hurt in this week's attacks. CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper met Israel's military chief in Tel Aviv, and Haaretz reports that Israel is seeking US backing for renewed strikes on Iran. Three US carrier strike groups are in the region.
items.notes: The Qeshm strike was partly covered on Nov 18. Iranian state media says it caused no serious damage. The Haaretz link is paywalled.

items.text: Punchbowl News reports that a government shutdown at the Dec 11 deadline is growing more likely. Speaker Johnson and Majority Leader Thune reject any deal that limits Trump's conduct of the Iran war, while Schumer and Jeffries say they need Iran language to agree. Thune called curbs on Iran-war funding 'not a realistic ask'. Rep. Rosa DeLauro favours a short stopgap into February, when Democrats will hold both chambers. Senate Democrats are split, and retiring members and some red-state senators are wary of a hardline strategy. Congress leaves for Thanksgiving after this week and returns Nov 30.
items.notes: ABC/AP report a separate House GOP push for a $95bn package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities, but that article could not be read. The Washington Times (right-leaning) frames Democrats as debating how to block the funding without a shutdown.

items.text: The Justice Department filed an emergency application on Wednesday asking the Supreme Court, for the third time, to halt a ruling by US District Judge Edward Chen that restores Temporary Protected Status for Venezuelans. The ruling is due to take effect Friday. The administration says reinstatement would block up to 332 removal orders, force it to issue work permits, and could free about 1,800 detained Venezuelans, Al Jazeera reports. The Biden administration had extended TPS for about 600,000 Venezuelans, and the Supreme Court paused an earlier Chen ruling in 2025.
items.notes: The Washington Post (AP) link is paywalled.

items.text: US District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended by 14 days, to Dec 3, the temporary restraining order blocking construction of Trump's memorial arch at Memorial Circle in Washington, the AP reports. She said nothing material had changed since her Nov 5 order. The extension holds until Dec 3 or until she rules on a pending preliminary-injunction request, whichever comes first. The administration argues that Congress long ago authorised a monument at the site, while plaintiffs say new congressional approval is needed.
items.notes: This is a separate case from the East Potomac Park TRO before Judge Reyes (W-261116-02).

items.text: In a communiqué on Nov 18 (reported by PAP), the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) General Assembly convened by Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska said it had lifted TK President Bogdan Święczkowski's immunity in four cases: repeated delegation of nine prosecutors while he was National Prosecutor, abuse linked to the Pegasus investigation, blocking five judges from adjudicating, and an alleged physical assault on Judge Maciej Berek on Oct 14. It refused consent to detain or arrest him, but suspended him from duties and cut his pay by 50%. It also allowed the prosecution of Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański (blocking judges, violating employee rights), suspending him with a 25% pay cut. Prosecutor General Waldemar Żurek wrote that charges can now be brought; Święczkowski said no valid assembly took place, he is not suspended, he will not answer summonses, and the 'legitimate' judges will work 'in exile' for a time.
items.notes: Six judges, including Sochański, Piotrowicz and Wyrembak, say the assembly was unauthorised and inquorate (nczas.info, right-leaning). Supreme Court First President Kapiński said the law is broken 'at every step'. No vote count was published in the sources read. No attempt to detain Święczkowski was reported.

items.text: Three combined Supreme Court chambers (Civil; Labour and Social Insurance; Extraordinary Control and Public Affairs), with more than 40 judges mostly appointed after 2017, adopted a resolution on Nov 18 on a question from Civil Chamber President Joanna Misztal-Konecka. It says a valid TK ruling is one issued by a panel made up only of judges who took their oath before the President, and that such rulings are binding even if the government does not publish them in the official journal. Prawo.pl notes about 85 TK rulings remain unpublished, and five of the eight new TK judges took their oath in the Sejm, not before the President. Deputy Justice Minister Dariusz Mazur called the reports disinformation, arguing that people not entitled to sit as Supreme Court judges cannot change the law.
items.notes: TVN24 stresses that most of the judges are KRS appointees after 2017, which the government does not recognise. Right-leaning headlines (DoRzeczy, Tysol) call it a breakthrough that undermines the 'takeover' of the TK; those full articles could not be fetched. Justice Minister Żurek also rejected it, per the PAP Biznes digest.

items.text: The second round of talks on the TK crisis, chaired by the President's chief of staff Zbigniew Bogucki, took place on Nov 18 with PiS, PSL, Polska 2050, Konfederacja, Razem, Rozwój Plus, Konfederacja Korony Polskiej and Demokracja Bezpośrednia; KO and the Left again stayed away. Bogucki said the parties agree on about 70% of issues in a joint Chancellery draft constitutional amendment, based on PSL's proposal and supplemented by other clubs. He said the remaining 30%, the transitional measures to end the crisis, may be the hardest part. A third meeting is set for Thursday Nov 19 at 18:00.
items.notes: An amendment needs a two-thirds Sejm majority, which is not reachable without KO. Earlier TVN24 coverage quoted Left MP Tomasz Trela saying one does not negotiate with 'constitutional terrorists'. No draft text has been published.

items.text: Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz confirmed a Rzeczpospolita report that, in late October and early November, Polish special services, police and elite army units ran a secret preventive and deterrent operation that foiled a planned Russian sabotage provocation near the border with Russia's Kaliningrad region. Speaking in Jarosław on Nov 18, he said the services knew of the preparations and that many sabotage attempts have been foiled. He warned that Russia could also stage provocations on the Baltic states' borders, and announced a request to the PM and the President to extend Operation Horyzont, in which the army helps protect infrastructure including railways.
items.notes: The nature and location of the planned provocation were not disclosed. The original Rzeczpospolita investigation is paywalled; TVN24 and other outlets carried the PAP account.

items.text: President Nawrocki vetoed a law that would have raised VAT from 5% (8% in gastronomy) to 23% on energy drinks with caffeine or taurine, 0.0% beer, drinks up to 0.5% alcohol, and non-alcoholic alternatives containing at least 20% juice. Money.pl puts the lost revenue at about 1.3bn zł in 2027 and 15.8bn zł over 2027–2036. He signed the excise amendment raising duties on alcohol, beer, wine, intermediate products and cider from 2027, with the extra money guaranteed for the NFZ health fund as he had requested. The PAP Biznes digest says he also signed a law scrapping the internet tax relief, expanding the blood-donor relief and extending the robotisation relief by a decade.
items.thread: Poland public finances and credit ratings
items.notes: Farmer.pl reports that the President cited signals from farmers and fruit growers (juice-based drinks); not read in full. The PIT-relief signing is single-source (PAP Biznes digest via Strefa Inwestorów); TVP Info says three laws were signed in total.

items.text: On Nov 18 the Sejm Health Committee recommended rejecting four Senate amendments to the anti-alcohol law: allowing 0% beer advertising (2 for, 26 against), craft-beer events on wine-event terms, airport and free-zone exemptions from the 22:00–06:00 night sales ban, and advertising in wholesale and liquor stores. It backed allowing sponsorship information at sports events (not school sports clubs), a clarified definition of promotion, selling off non-compliant packaging, moving entry into force from Jan 1 to Jun 1, 2027, and extending the deadline for removing logos from fridges to end-2030. The Health Ministry opposed the rejected amendments. The Sejm votes during the current sitting.
items.notes: Rejecting a Senate amendment needs an absolute majority in the Sejm. The voting block is Nov 19, 10:45–13:00.

items.text: The Sejm Health Committee on Nov 18 rejected a Senate amendment cutting the minimum employment needed at a facility from half to a quarter of a full-time post, but backed the Senate's removal of sanctions (up to an 8-year ban from public-system work) for doctors who falsify records, prescriptions or sick notes. The Sejm votes on Nov 19. The bill caps pay in 2027 at about 247 zł gross an hour and a total of about 79.2k zł a month (16 times the minimum wage), with a 320-hour monthly limit. The committee chair flagged a possible presidential veto on constitutional grounds.
items.notes: Razem's Marcelina Zawisza opposes dropping the sanctions, so the floor outcome is uncertain.

items.text: UOKiK, the competition and consumer authority, fined Allegro 54.73m zł for greenwashing: 29.85m zł over its Allegro One 'one tree for 10 parcels' promise and 24.88m zł for not properly disclosing the conditions. UOKiK found that some trees were planted based on forecasts or before customers were assigned to them, and some were never planted. Customers also had to collect 10 parcels within a calendar year and, from 2024, submit a tree dedication through a panel option that was long disabled. The decision is appealable.
items.notes: No Allegro response or appeal decision was found in the sources read. The same day, Allegro raised its maximum buyback price to 65 zł a share.

items.text: The National Prosecutor's Office charged three more people in the Zondacrypto (formerly BitBay) crypto-exchange case after the CBZC cybercrime bureau detained them on Nov 17, and asked the Warsaw-Mokotów court to remand them. According to spokeswoman Anna Adamiak, they are a lawyer accused of preparing reports with false information on how client assets were secured, a former finance director accused of approving unauthorised transfers from client funds, and former BitBay co-shareholder Jacek R., who ran IT and allegedly gave unauthorised people access to user accounts. Each faces charges including membership of an organised criminal group; none admitted guilt.
items.notes: The sources give no total loss or number of victims.

items.text: Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka said on Nov 18 that a draft raising the share of gas that must be sold on the commodity exchange from 55% to 80% is at the final stage before the government's Standing Committee and may be adopted this year. He said the aim is a more transparent market, linked to lower transmission charges. He also said proposals to shield households from higher 2027 electricity bills will come in the coming weeks. ING estimates that freezing both gas and electricity prices for 2027 would cut average inflation by about 0.7 percentage points.
items.notes: The ING figure and the electricity remarks come from the PAP Biznes digest.

items.text: Eurostat data show Poland's HICP inflation eased to 3.7% year on year in October from 4.0%. According to PAP Biznes, NBP First Deputy President Marta Kightley told the Sejm that the supply shock is self-limiting but rate hikes could be used to anchor inflation expectations, and MPC member Marcin Zarzecki said the Council may be forced to hike in Q1 2027. MPC member Ireneusz Dąbrowski saw no need for hikes, citing the November NBP projection of inflation returning to target.
items.notes: Bankier's Kightley article could not be fetched; the MPC quotes rely on the digest.

items.text: Joint Sejm committees suspended work on an MPs' bill (print 3295) from Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski and Marshal Włodzimierz Czarzasty. It would move a one-off 1.5bn zł from defence spending to the Polish Science Fund to build domestic chip production lines, including at the CEZAMAT facility. The Defence Ministry said it cannot spare the money in 2026 or 2027, and the rapporteur filed many amendments the Legislative Bureau had no time to review. MPs said the coalition must first agree on funding; no new committee date is set. The bill targets 3bn zł of investment by 2030 and doubling chip specialists to about 3,000.
items.notes: Conflict: the PAP Biznes evening digest (Strefa Inwestorów, Nov 18) says the semiconductor bill 'passed committee'. Nauka w Polsce (PAP, Nov 18) and CyberDefence24 say work was suspended; the more detailed accounts are used here.

items.text: The Grudziądz city office said on Nov 18 that residents can use ePUAP again after the nationwide shutdown that followed the foreign cyberattack. The government says restoration is phased, and some functions may stay unavailable until maintenance ends. No new national statement from the Digital Affairs Ministry on full restoration, attribution or the ABW investigation was found for Nov 18.
items.notes: Local source only; treat as a sign of partial national restoration, not a confirmation. No new information on the Autopay breach (number affected) was found.

items.text: PM Donald Tusk will represent Poland at Thursday's (Nov 19) Berlin meeting of the 'coalition of the willing' convened by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, with Volodymyr Zelensky, Alexander Stubb and Andrej Babiš among those attending. The agenda covers aid to Ukraine, post-war security guarantees and coordinating the peace talks; US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected in Berlin. Poland is part of a new European negotiating team agreed in Dublin and represented by Robert Kupiecki; the Kremlin says it has not accepted European participation.
items.notes: Preview article; the meeting's outcome is due later on Nov 19.

items.text: Kraków City Council did not adopt Mayor Łukasz Gibała's draft resolution suspending the partnership with Lviv (druk 1586). A majority of KO and Nowa Lewica councillors voted instead to send the draft back to the mayor, while PiS and the mayor's club Kraków dla Mieszkańców voted against returning it, according to Rzeczpospolita. KO councillors say Gibała should first ask Lviv Mayor Andriy Sadovyi again for his position on the Lviv regional council naming 2027 the 'Year of the UPA'. Gibała wrote on X that he is keeping the motion and that Sadovyi has not replied to his letter.
items.thread: Kraków–Lviv partnership and the Year of the UPA
items.notes: Neither source gives vote tallies. Newsmax Polska (right-leaning) builds its story on Gibała's X post and presents Sadovyi's silence as a snub. Rzeczpospolita leads with the council majority's procedural reasoning. Gazeta Krakowska also reported the result (headline: councillors did not back the proposal), but its page could not be fetched.

items.text: The fare resolution bringing back the 20-minute (4 zł) ticket (druk 1587) was not voted on at the 18 November session. Kurier Krakowski reports that the council's Infrastructure Committee did not give its opinion on the draft because consultations and formalities ran long, so the vote moves to the December session. According to the draft on BIP, the resolution would take effect on 4 January 2027, cost about 19.6m zł a year in lost revenue, and extend the student annual ticket to doctoral students. Fines would be set as multiples of the 20-minute fare: 400 zł for riding without a ticket.
items.notes: Kurier Krakowski reported the postponement on 16 Nov, but the 18 Nov log still listed the item as due. A Dziennik Polski headline (decision postponed, key date unchanged) agrees; its page could not be fetched. Kurier Krakowski gives 1 Jan 2027 as the start date, while the BIP draft says 4 Jan 2027. No exact December session date has been confirmed.

items.text: The nine resolutions on Kraków leaving organisations, including EUROCITIES, Małopolska Tourist Organisation, Kraków Tourism Alliance, the Jurassic Municipalities Union and the Association of Municipalities and Counties of Małopolska, were removed from the 18 November session agenda with the support of all councillors present, KRKnews reported. Councillor Aleksandra Owca said the relevant department is to deliver a cost-benefit comparison within two weeks, after which councillors will assess each membership. The mayor's office puts the savings from leaving at about 8.2m zł a year.
items.thread: Kraków city finances and the 2027 budget
items.notes: From a KRKnews live blog. A Dziennik Polski headline (councillors want hard data on leaving tourism organisations) points the same way, but its page could not be fetched.

items.text: Councillors clashed at the session over the draft freezing Clean Transport Zone (SCT) entry fees at 100 zł a month, 5 zł a day or 2.50 zł an hour until the end of the transition period. Tomasz Leśniak called the consultations a sham and a joke. Grzegorz Garboliński said the freeze mainly helps drivers from outside Kraków, and KO's Grzegorz Stawowy questioned giving up revenue while the city is looking for savings. Deputy Mayor Jan Hoffman admitted the online survey cannot verify residence and said the freeze was split off because the higher fees would otherwise start on 1 January. PiS councillor Michał Drewnicki called the freeze a return to normality.
items.notes: No vote was held; the draft is still in consultation until 27 Nov.

items.text: KO and Nowa Lewica councillors are seeking an extraordinary council session, which they want next week, on Mayor Gibała's decision to stop funding metro preparations and remove the money from the multi-year financial forecast. KO club chair Grzegorz Stawowy said the club wants the analyses behind the decision and the status of the two tenders (geological survey and preparatory documentation, including a feasibility study), including any risk of contractual penalties. Deputy Mayor Karol Wałachowski repeated that the city will not pay for preparing an investment with no funding and will develop trams instead.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Kurier Krakowski's headline links the dispute to as much as 60m zł in SCT money; that page was not read in full. No date for the session yet.

items.text: Eryk Stasielak, head of the National Prosecutor's Office branch in Małopolska, told Onet that the officers who shot the 7 November attacker were wearing body cameras that were recording; prosecutors call the footage key evidence and will not describe it. More than 100 cartridge cases were found in the attacker's car, along with four phones. One phone was dead and may have locked itself, but Stasielak expects it to be opened. A safe at the attacker's home held ammunition and other items still under analysis. Nothing found so far points to a motive.
items.notes: TVN24 is relaying an Onet interview, with PAP also credited.

items.text: At the start of the council session, Mayor Gibała presented 'Honoris Gratia' badges to nearly 30 doctors, nurses and paramedics who helped victims of the 7 November attack. Recipients included Prof. Michał Pędziwiatr, paramedics from the Kraków ambulance service, and the Slovak day-trippers Linda Trnková and Mário Mačina. The session opened with a minute's silence for the victims and for former councillor Stanisław Kozak.

Deputy Mayor Karol Wałachowski has signed a notification to prosecutors about contracts worth more than 300,000 zł between the Sports Infrastructure Authority (ZIS) and the PR agency Mais Group for promotion and media relations. KRKnews, citing Radio Kraków, says a city audit questioned outsourcing work that ZIS staff, including its own spokesperson, could have done. The notification follows the dismissal of ZIS director Tomasz Marzec on 27 October.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: KRKnews credits Radio Kraków as the original source.

items.text: The city cleaning company MPO, which runs Kraków's 2026/27 winter maintenance, says 286 machines and more than 12,000 tonnes of salt are ready. They cover 1,481 km of roads, 810 km of pavements and 201 km of bike paths, with main transit routes cleared first. The season is budgeted at about 62.6m zł, based on the five-year average, against 39.7m zł spent last winter. Residents can report problems to the MPO dispatch on 12 64 62 361.

IMD says Akvan became a severe cyclonic storm at 05:30 IST on Nov 18. Late on Nov 18 it was about 480 km southeast of Narsapur, moving slowly north-northwest. IMD expects it to cross the north Andhra Pradesh–Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri around noon to afternoon on Nov 20. Forecasts for landfall winds now vary by outlet: ANI cites 90–100 km/h gusting to 110, while Business Standard cites 120–130 km/h gusting to 145 after a possible upgrade to very severe on the evening of Nov 19. Red alerts cover seven coastal AP districts (Kakinada-Yanam, East and West Godavari, Konaseema, Eluru, Krishna, Bapatla). The AP disaster authority has 13 NDRF and 11 SDRF teams on standby, and ANI reports three trains rescheduled.
items.notes: Intensity forecasts differ. Business Standard and Swarajya (Nov 18) say a very severe cyclonic storm is expected by the evening of Nov 19, with gusts up to 145 km/h. The ANI/NewsBytes reports of Nov 19 give landfall winds of only 90–110 km/h, which may mean a downgraded forecast. One ANI headline says 'by noon' without a date; other reports put landfall on Nov 20. No deaths reported. ANI pages could not be fetched, so the ANI details come via NewsBytes and the search snippets.

items.text: The Odisha government has evacuated nearly 50,000 people from vulnerable areas ahead of Cyclone Akvan, NewsBytes reports. That is part of the roughly 2.04 lakh identified as at risk. Schools and anganwadi centres in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal are closed from Nov 19 to 21, and a red warning covers 13 districts. CM Mohan Charan Majhi warned of heavy rain in southern and coastal districts. The state has also suspended sea tourism and boating at vulnerable coastal spots and begun releasing water from the Harabhangi and Badanalla dams.
items.notes: The 50,000 evacuation figure and the school closures come from NewsBytes (aggregating ANI) only. Business Standard (Nov 18) gives the 2.04 lakh planning figure and says more than 100 pregnant women had already been moved.

items.text: The Sensex fell 500.38 points (0.61%) to 82,031.81 and the Nifty 159.45 points (0.63%) to 25,227.95 on Nov 18, ending a two-day rise. Business Standard attributes the fall to profit-taking, weak global cues and a stronger dollar on expectations of further Fed hikes. Consumer durables (−3.1%) and metals (−2.5%) led the decline, and the Nifty Midcap 100 lost 1.2%. Brent stayed below $95 a barrel, and the rupee closed at about 93.44 per dollar.

The IPO of Mahanadi Coalfields, a Coal India subsidiary, opens for subscription on Nov 19 and closes on Nov 23, after anchor bidding on Nov 18. The issue is a pure offer for sale of a 10% stake by Coal India, worth about ₹8,981 crore at a price band of ₹129–136. At the top of the band it values MCL at about ₹90,000 crore, roughly 8.4 times FY26 profit. Grey-market premiums of about ₹10–13 a share were reported before opening.
items.notes: Anchor allocation results were not found. One report calls this Coal India's third subsidiary listing this year (not verified).

items.text: The ECI has extended the ASDD (absent, shifted, dead, duplicate) verification schedule in seven states and UTs: Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Delhi, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Nagaland and Haryana, IANS reports. Door-to-door distribution and collection of enumeration forms will run from Nov 18 to 30, with processing due by Dec 10 and claims and objections by Dec 15. Final rolls will now be published on Dec 22 instead of Nov 30. The commission says the extension is meant to strengthen verification of ASDD-category voters.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: The ECI order itself was not found; the date of the order is not stated. Separately, LiveLaw reports that petitioners in the Delhi SIR case cited a report on misuse of Form 7 (deletion objections) in the Supreme Court on Nov 18.

items.text: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav led a roughly 20-km 'PDA Rath Yatra' roadshow on Nov 18 from Gorakhpur airport to Deokahi in Chauri Chaura, CM Yogi Adityanath's home turf (PTI). Supporters greeted him with bulldozers. According to Outlook, he predicted the BJP would win none of the nine Gorakhpur-area seats it swept in 2022 and alleged attempts to delete about 31,000 votes per constituency. He also called Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya a 'fake Sanatani'. Maurya said the yatra was meant to mislead backward classes and Dalits, and UP BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary told Akhilesh to hold a 'repentance march' for the 2012–17 SP government.
items.notes: The vote-deletion figure is Akhilesh's claim and its unit is unclear in the Outlook account. PTI's pre-event report says local BJP figure Ajay Kumar Singh 'Tappu' was expected to join the SP; that has not been confirmed. Prabhasakshi says the SP claimed a crowd of 1 lakh.

items.text: Speaking at Columbia University in New York during a two-day US visit, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi said India is 'sitting on an economic disaster', with serious unemployment and education problems. He said frustrated young middle-class Indians cannot see a future for themselves. BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari called him the 'Leader of Anti-India Propaganda' and cited India's status as the fastest-growing major economy. Congress replied that the government cares more about Gandhi's remarks than about the economy. He is due at the University of Chicago next.
items.notes: The Congress response is taken from a Deccan Herald headline, since the article could not be fetched.

items.text: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar arrived in Tokyo on Nov 18 for the fourth India–Japan 2+2 ministerial dialogue with Shinjiro Koizumi and Toshimitsu Motegi, running Nov 18–19. The MoD says the agenda covers defence equipment and technology, maritime security, larger tri-service exercises and industrial partnerships. Opening Raisina Tokyo 2026, Jaishankar urged Japanese business to 'update the picture of India'. He named semiconductors, critical minerals, AI, clean energy and pharmaceuticals as areas for cooperation. The visit comes days after the JIMEX naval exercise (Nov 13–14).
items.notes: As of the morning of Nov 19 (Warsaw), no outcome document had been found.

items.text: The 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit (Nov 17–19, theme 'AI & Beyond') saw Karnataka launch six initiatives. They include a Karnataka AI Hub and BRAINZ, with ARTPARK at IISc, which aims to attract ₹1,000 crore over five years. Others are a '2D Innovation Hub' proposing a national 200-mm semiconductor R&D fab and pilot line, and the INFIfab advanced-packaging cleanroom. CM D.K. Shivakumar announced a state-backed AI University and AI teaching from primary school, without giving funding or a timeline. CareerIndia reports MoUs with Google, Salesforce, Pega, Sarvam AI and Gnani.ai, and a skilling target of 63,200 learners. An India–US Tech Conclave on quantum, critical minerals, secure AI and cybersecurity was held on Nov 18.
items.notes: No Karnataka government release was found; the figures come from secondary outlets. Tech Times calls Nov 17 a Monday, but it was a Tuesday. No outcomes were found from the India–US conclave.

items.text: At the close of the first Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians India Region conference at Bengaluru's Vidhana Soudha on Nov 18, Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav said deepfakes and online harassment threaten women's safety and participation in public life (PTI). She called for stronger legal safeguards and platform accountability. Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh made similar points. CWP India chair D. Purandeswari said women's digital empowerment and digital safety cannot be treated separately. The conference drew more than 150 delegates.
items.notes: This comes as MeitY's promised AI-regulation consultation paper, which covers deepfakes, still had not been published as of Nov 19 despite the minister's early-November target.

items.text: The Delhi Police IFSO unit arrested three men in Lucknow over a 'digital arrest' scam in which a 66-year-old retired Defence Ministry section officer was pressured into transferring about ₹2.02 crore (IANS). The callers told him an account had been opened in J&K with his Aadhaar details and that he was under investigation. Police say the accused supplied and ran mule accounts and moved commissions through USDT cryptocurrency. They seized phones, debit cards and a cheque book.
items.notes: The Supreme Court's suo motu digital-arrest case (platform anti-scam proposals) is due around Nov 23 (W-261111-04).

items.text: LiveLaw reports several Supreme Court orders on Nov 18. The court issued notice on a plea to finalise the Memorandum of Procedure for judicial appointments and bring collegium minutes under the RTI Act. It reserved judgment on raising district judges' retirement age (All India Judges Association). It declined for now to stay Azam Khan's interim bail on the ED's plea, listing it for the next day. It also held that a stay of conviction cannot be sought solely in order to contest elections. CJI Surya Kant met the UN Special Rapporteur on disability rights and said the court will set up a disability-rights committee.
items.notes: Based only on LiveLaw headlines and teasers; the full reports are paywalled, and benches were not identified.

items.text: Ladakh State Election Commissioner Sudhanshu Pandey reviewed preparations in Leh on Nov 17 for the Nov 21 panchayat and municipal polls: polling stations, staff, security and logistics. The review followed one by Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra on Nov 16 (PTI). The hill council (LAHDC) polls remain set for Dec 4. The Leh Apex Body, Kargil Democratic Alliance and several religious and local groups oppose the winter timing, and some have announced boycotts.
items.thread: Ladakh statehood protests and council polls
items.notes: No postponement had been announced as of Nov 19. The boycott list comes from a Nov 13 report.

items.text: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Nov 18, at a curtain-raiser for FICCI's annual general meeting in New Delhi, that almost every element of the interim India–US trade agreement is settled. He added that it cannot be signed until Washington puts its new tariff 'architecture' in place. He said countries will want clarity on the outcome of the US Section 301 investigations before signing, because the new US tariff rules will decide how Indian exporters compete with rivals. The February framework had envisaged an 18% US tariff on Indian goods, but the Supreme Court later struck down the emergency-powers tariffs it relied on. Agrawal also said India is on track for $1 trillion in exports this fiscal year.
items.notes: The same remarks were carried by IANS Hindi, Amar Ujala and Aaj Tak (Nov 19). Bloomberg ran it as 'nearly ready, signing may take time' (not fetched: robots-blocked). This makes signing depend on the US Section 301 outcomes, not only on the negotiations themselves.

items.text: The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule on Nov 16 requiring licences to export, re-export or transfer advanced AI chips to overseas data centres that give significant computing power (above 12 million TPP) to firms headquartered in China, Macau or other arms-embargoed countries. Separate country licences are now needed for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, but not for India. Indian trade press frames this as an edge over regional rivals for AI data-centre investment. Indian operators would still need customer checks (KYC) to show they are not serving restricted firms, according to a Moneycontrol report. The rule formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule, is due in the Federal Register on Nov 19 and opens a 60-day comment period; existing data centres have 90 days to obtain licences.
items.notes: Late catch: the rule was issued Nov 16 but did not appear in earlier logs, and Indian coverage ran Nov 17–18. The rule itself (a US regulation) may also be logged by the US slice; this entry covers the India angle. Communications Today names Yotta's GPU deployment and Reliance's Jamnagar AI build-out as India's main exposure, through delivery timelines.

items.text: India and the US held the 23rd meeting of their Military Cooperation Group in New Delhi on Nov 17–18, according to IANS, citing a post by India's Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff. Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, Chief of Integrated Defence Staff, and Lt Gen George B. Rowell of US Indo-Pacific Command co-chaired it. They discussed emerging military domains and defence technologies, deeper cyber cooperation, joint exercises, battlefield medical support and logistics under the 2025 Major Defence Partnership framework. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to interoperability.
items.notes: The IANS headline says the sides 'agreed' on cyber and emerging tech, but the body only says these were discussed. No PIB/MoD release was found by this run, and the HQ IDS post was not seen directly.

items.text: The seventh Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation (P-TEC) ministerial opened in Warsaw on Nov 18 (through Nov 19). It is co-organised by the US Energy Department, Poland's Energy Ministry and the Atlantic Council, and brings in US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and representatives of more than 20 European countries. PM Donald Tusk met Wright and Ambassador Tom Rose, and in a gala speech called the Poland–Europe–US relationship an 'axis of good'. Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka named long-term US gas contracts as a priority and cast Poland as a gateway for US gas to the region. Wright called Poland a strategic ally and told TVN24 that a 2036 start for Poland's first nuclear unit, being built with US firms, is realistic if approvals stay on schedule. No contracts were reported on day one.
items.notes: Wright's 2036 remark is from a TVN24 BiS interview (https://tvn24.pl/biznes/z-kraju/co-z-elektrownia-jadrowa-w-polsce-sekretarz-energii-chris-wright-rok-2036-to-bedzie-realny-termin-st9345898). Motyka also used the forum to call for delaying EU ETS2. The ministerial day (Nov 19) could bring LNG or nuclear announcements.

items.text: Poland's state development fund PFR and the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) signed a cooperation declaration at the P-TEC meeting in Warsaw on Nov 18. Under it they will look for ways to draw private capital into nuclear power and other strategic energy projects, including gas infrastructure. They will also assess how DFC equity, loans and guarantees could be used. PFR president Mikołaj Raczyński called nuclear one of the biggest investment challenges of the coming decades, and Finance Minister Andrzej Domański said the government wants private capital in the nuclear programme. PFR says it is neutral on technology supplier, and no amounts were announced.
items.notes: The PAP Biznes evening roundup also carried it. The pfr.pl press release could not be fetched. WNP notes the second large nuclear plant's site (Bełchatów or Konin) and supplier (Westinghouse, EDF or AtkinsRéalis) are due in H2 2027. A declaration, not a financing commitment.

items.text: The same Nov 16 US Commerce rule on remote access to advanced chips formally rescinds the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule and its country tiers. That rule had left Poland outside the group of closest US allies with unrestricted access to advanced GPUs, which caused a diplomatic row in Warsaw in 2025. BIS says the Diffusion Rule was never enforced (it was suspended in May 2025), so the practical change for Poland is formal rather than immediate. No European country is among the five named for new licence requirements. Polish-American outlet Dziennik Polonijny reported the rule on Nov 18.
items.notes: No Polish government reaction was found. The Poland link is contextual: the 2025 tier placement was the issue Warsaw lobbied on.
